_note: Our own writing. Mid-mission twists: the book says a mission's goal can change when new information comes to light (Core p.43). A hook may carry one (hidden from the briefing); the GM reveals it during the mission (gm_twist events, ask for src/gm) and the debrief applies its consequence. 'chance' = how often a hook rolls a twist at all. Effects use StoryEffects; $hook.faction = the patron's faction, $hook.rival = the other side of the hub's conflict.

reveal: The cargo isn't what {patron} said it was.
The job was never what it seemed: {patron} was moving weapons, and knew it.
Your orders were written to keep you from asking questions.
twists.question: Do you finish the job anyway, now that you know?

reveal: An enemy pilot is broadcasting on an open channel: they want out.
One of the opposing mechs powers down and raises its arms.
twists.question: Can you get the defector out alive?

reveal: A third force drops in, and they aren't on anyone's side.
New transponders on the scope. Not {enemy}. Someone else wants this too.
twists.question: Who sent them, and what do they want here?

reveal: There are people sheltering in the target area. Nobody said there would be.
Civilian vehicles on the road, right in the line of fire.
twists.question: Will you change the plan to keep them safe?

reveal: This was a diversion. The real strike is happening somewhere else right now.
The enemy wanted you here. Their actual target is behind you.
twists.question: Can you get back in time to matter?

reveal: An NHP is running the enemy's systems, and it's asking you questions.
The thing you came to recover is a casket, and someone is awake inside it.
twists.question: What do you owe a mind that didn't choose this fight?

reveal: You know those paint schemes. The same squad you met before.
A lancer team you've crossed paths with is fighting for the other side.
twists.question: Is this where your rivalry ends?

reveal: A storm front rolls in, faster than forecast. Sensors go to static.
The ground starts to give way: the whole area is undermined.
twists.question: Can you finish before the world itself turns on you?

reveal: Someone on the inside opens a gate for you, and won't say why.
A message arrives on a private channel: patrol routes, door codes, a name.
twists.question: Who is helping you, and what will they want for it?

obligation.what: A favor for whoever opened the gate

reveal: New orders, mid-drop: hold position instead of advancing.
Command changes the objective: the target is now to be taken intact.
twists.question: Will you follow the new orders, or your own judgment?

reveal: Someone tampered with your mechs before the drop. Little things, but enough.
A diagnostic flags a fault that wasn't there this morning. Sabotage.
twists.question: Who had access to the printer bay?

reveal: The enemy commander calls for a ceasefire and offers terms.
A white flag goes up over the enemy line. They want to talk.
twists.question: Do you accept their surrender, and can you trust it?

reveal: Another lancer squad is pinned down nearby and calling for help.
Friendly transponders, close and failing. Someone's in trouble.
twists.question: Do you divert to help, or stick to the plan?

reveal: The enemy knew your route. Someone told them.
They were waiting. Your plan was leaked.
twists.question: Who leaked the plan?

reveal: In the wreckage: an intact cache nobody listed in the briefing.
One of the enemy carriers was hauling something valuable.
twists.question: Who does the prize belong to?

effects.name: What you found in the wreckage

reveal: Someone you trust has been reporting your moves to the enemy.
A friendly voice on the comms is feeding the enemy your positions.
twists.question: What do you do with a traitor?

reveal: Before the squad is even out of {hub}, they're waiting outside {spot}. This fight happens in town.
You never make it to {place}: {enemy} are in the street outside {spot}, and they've seen you.
twists.question: Who told them where you'd be?
